The paper demonstrates that technology alone cannot save a civilization: increasing N without reducing D amplifies D, not V. The only passage through the Great Filter is D→0 — the deliberate, systematic reduction of friction at civilizational scale. The paper introduces the concept of the Superconducting Civilization (a D→0 phase transition state) and presents the Hikari Engine as the first operational proof of concept for D→0 infrastructure. The universe is silent not because life is rare, but because the denominator wins.

The paper argues that the difference between these futures is not destiny but design — a choice being made in this decade.

title: Agent-Readable Web Design Theory: Design Principles for AI-Accessible Websites
abstract: As AI agents become primary consumers of web content, the distinction between human-readable and agent-readable websites has become critical. This paper reports experimental findings from a real-world case study on theykhc.com, demonstrating that JavaScript-rendered websites (e.g., Wix) are largely invisible to AI crawlers, while static HTML and JSON endpoints remain fully accessible. We propose five design principles for agent-readable web architecture and introduce the concept of AX (Agent Experience) as a new design layer alongside UX and CX.
keywords: AI agent, web design, AX, Agent Experience, static HTML, JSON-LD, crawlability, LLM, Wix, GitHub Pages
